Elsa: Heads-up — big tail latency regression observed on canary after merge 0f3a2c5. p99 up ~2.8x on INT8 profile. Holding the canary now. :eyes:
Elsa: Quick snapshot from prod-canary logs shows requests stalling in dequant path during decode.
Elsa: log excerpt:
```
2026-03-18T09:12:21Z decode loop: dequantize_int8 + matmul spike
request_id=... latency=1.9s p99 prev=0.7s
stack: runtime::dequantize_int8 -> runtime::kv_lookup -> runtime::matmul_int8
```
CI-bot: Perf CI: https://ci.redwood/teams/eng/runtime/jobs/bert-int8-perf/987 FAILED — regression +18% vs baseline.
Michael: I ran a quick flamegraph on canary instance. dequantize_int8 accounts for ~70% CPU time during decode. gist: https://gist.github.com/michael/fg-dequant (flamegraph).
Raj: Noticed KV cache miss-rate doubled for same workload after the merge. On misses we end up re-dequantizing keys each time, so miss amplification looks bad.
Sophie: Did that merge change kernel selection heuristics? I recall PR 0f3a2c5 adjusted "prefer_small_block" for kernel selector to help batchy workloads. That could make us choose a generic dequant path that does extra memcpy.
Michael: I did a quick git bisection locally: regression introduced between 0e9b... and 0f3a2c5. Candidate PR is 4492 (quant-kernel-selector-heuristic). Bisect result: good before 4492, bad after.
Elsa: Local repro with sequence_len=1024, batch=1 reproduces the hotspot. pprof -top shows:
```
pprof -top cpu.prof
  dequantize_int8   71.4%  (hot)
  matmul_int8       12.2%
  kv_cache_lookup    8.9%
  memcpy             5.1%
```
Raj: Additional detail: the new selector favors a small-block kernel that is not fused with dequant; that kernel expects dequantized data and so we run an explicit dequant memcpy+convert step. Previously the selector chose a fused dequant+matmul kernel that avoided the extra copy.
Sophie: That explains the CPU and memory traffic. For long sequences + KV cache churn the extra memcpy dominates. We also lack telemetry for "dequant copy counts" per request.
Michael: Short-term mitigation: flip the runtime flag to restore old selector on canary: `redwoodctl set-config runtime.use_new_kernel_selector=false --target canary`. I can push that in 10m.
CI-bot: action required: perf gate failing will block merge queue until resolved.
Elsa: Agree short-term revert/flag flip. I'll open a revert PR for 4492 and a follow-up to reintroduce the heuristic only when batch_size>1 or seq_len<256.
Sophie: Long-term: add a fused dequant+matmul kernel or detection in selector (prefer fused when kv_cache_hit_rate>0.9 or seq_len>512). Also add microbenchmarks and a dequant telemetry metric.
Raj: I'll add KV cache telemetry (hit/miss by sequence_len) and a dequant-copy counter to the runtime. That should help catch this in CI.
Michael: I'll prepare a hotfix branch that forces fused kernel selection for int8 decode paths and add a unit perf test that runs the 1024-seq decode scenario in CI.
Elsa: Plan: 1) flip flag on canary now 2) open revert PR for 4492 3) hotfix fused-kernel branch + perf test 4) add telemetry and gating in CI. I'll assign follow-ups.
Sophie: ACK. Also add note to release notes: "reverted kernel selector tweak due to INT8 dequant overhead in long-sequence decode".
Elsa: Done holding canary and starting revert PR. Thanks all. :thumbsup: 
Michael: I filed the hotfix draft PR and linked the CI regression in the description. Ping me if you want to pair on the selector fallback. :+1:
Raj: Adding KV telemetry ticket to board now.
CI-bot: Note: blocked merges will be unblocked once perf gate passes on next canary run.
Elsa: Closing the loop here — we'll update this thread with PR numbers and canary metrics once available.
